# Failing Closed

What the review found, and the doors we shut.

## Every browser write carries a token

```html
<meta name="htmx-config"
      content='{"allowEval": false, "selfRequestsOnly": true}'>
<body hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token() }}"}'>
```

- **Every POST, PUT and DELETE from a session needs the token.** htmx adds it to every
  request from the page body.
- **The session cookie** is `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` in production; it lasts
  12 hours, and so does the token.
- **htmx only talks to us,** and never evaluates code.

† 14 routes are exempt: an API key has no cookie to forge. Seven are `…/refresh`, which also
take a session; a refresh is idempotent, so that trade-off is accepted.

::: {.notes}
src/webapp/templates/dashboards/base.html:18,30 (and a csrf-token meta tag at :9, which tests
read). Flask-WTF CSRFProtect: src/webapp/extensions.py:9,18, src/webapp/run.py:175-189 (a
failure returns JSON 400 under /api/, an htmx "session expired" fragment, or plain text).
#296, 2026-06-10, the first response to the NRIT review. Cookie flags: src/webapp/config.py:313-326,
353 (#105). WTF_CSRF_TIME_LIMIT=None, because the 1-hour default broke tabs left open. Exempt:
the status collectors (4), XRAS (3), and the refreshes for disk_quota, directory_access, queue,
project_access, wallclock_exemption, fstree_access and admin cache. Gate: tests/api/test_csrf.py.
:::

## One source of scripts: ours

```text
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'self'; object-src 'none';
base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
```

- Enforced from the first day, in June. `CSP_MODE=report-only` is the rollback, with no
  rebuild.
- No nonce: pages are cached per user, and a nonce would be stale on every hit. So no
  template holds an inline script; behavior lives in our own JavaScript files.
- A test scans every template. It started with 41 files of inline script; it allows none now.

† Built from the asset registry, so it cannot drift from what the pages load.

::: {.notes}
src/webapp/utils/csp.py:60-89 (the directives; trimmed here: font-src, connect-src, frame-src
are 'self'). Header set in src/webapp/utils/security_headers.py:30-62. #303, 2026-06-13: all
'self', vendored assets, enforce by default. The only widening: Cloudflare Turnstile (script and
frame) when configured, and the Google Calendar embed (frame). Inline styles are allowed:
they cannot run code (the review accepted it). Handlers are delegated data-action listeners;
per-swap setup runs in htmx.onLoad; data rides in non-executable JSON script blocks.
Ratchet: tests/unit/gates/test_template_csp_lint.py, seeded 2026-06-12 with 41 files,
ALLOWED_VIOLATIONS = {} now. It caught one real bug: a modal that closed itself with an inline
script stuck open; it now closes on an HX-Trigger header (2026-09-03). Other headers:
nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, CORP same-origin, Permissions-Policy
(#312), HSTS one year in production. Gates: tests/unit/webapp/test_csp.py,
test_security_headers.py.
:::

## No third-party origins {.vcenter scale="1.15"}

- Bootstrap 5.3.8, htmx 2.0.10, Font Awesome 7.3.1 and Poppins live in the repo, each pinned
  by its hash. CI re-hashes them.
- Why not a CDN: allowing one lets an injected script tag load any package it hosts. And
  browsers no longer share a CDN's cache between sites, so it isn't faster.
- Updates follow a skill: read the changelog against the workarounds we rely on, then bump.
  In September that bumped all four and dropped jQuery.

::: {.notes}
src/webapp/vendor_assets.py:28-62 (sha384 per entry point), templates use the vendor_css /
vendor_js macros. tests/unit/gates/test_vendor_assets.py re-hashes the committed files and
checks every asset is local. The browser checks no integrity attribute on local files; the
downloads were checked once against the publisher's hash, then CI holds the line.
src/webapp/static/vendor/README.md:9-19: self-hosting Poppins closed the one asset that could
never carry SRI. .claude/skills/update-vendored-assets/SKILL.md. #522-#524, 2026-09-07:
Bootstrap 5.3.3 to 5.3.8, htmx 2.0.4 to 2.0.10, Font Awesome 6 to 7.3.1, jQuery removed
(~87 KB a page; its one user rewritten in plain JS). htmx 4 is deferred as high-risk. #303
moved the first six CDN assets in, 2026-06-13.
:::

## Rate limits {.smaller .center .fill}

| Who | Limit | Per | Applies to |
|------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------|------------------------------------|
| **Signing in** | 5/min, 20/h | IP | login, the sign-in callback, registration |
| **Anonymous pages** | 30/min | IP | the front page, the login page |
| **Signed-in users** | 200/min | user | everything else |
| **API keys** | 120/min | IP | every key-only route |
| **Registration mail** | 3/h each; 10/h in all | email, site | the registration form |
| **The ingress** | 100/s, 200 open | site | everything |

† Counted in Redis; a 429 carries `Retry-After`. Health checks are never limited.

::: {.notes}
src/webapp/limiter/__init__.py (Flask-Limiter, fixed window; key order apikey, user, ip at
:35-53; Redis db 1, falls back to per-worker memory if Redis is down; the 429 handler at
:175-228 logs the actor and records it in ratelimit:events). Defaults = production:
src/webapp/config.py:85-92,186-192. API keys: src/webapp/utils/api_auth.py:220-224. Ingress:
helm/values.yaml:96-101, burst x5. #251 (2026-05-11), #316 (2026-06-16). Dev raises every tier
to 100,000/min except sign-in, so a load test there is real load. The dev load test sustained
121-180 requests a second from one address with no 429s (DEV_LOAD_CAMPAIGN.md:66-70): nginx
counts per worker process, so treat the ingress numbers as a floor. Admins can see and clear
blocks on the admin page.
:::

## ⚠︎ We can't see the client's address {.vcenter scale="1.15"}

- Every request arrives from 127.0.0.1. The address is lost before the app, and nothing on our
  side can recover it.
- So each per-IP limit is one bucket for everyone. One person's failed logins can lock everyone
  out of sign-in for the window.
- API keys too: their limit is checked before the key is known, so it counts per IP. All key
  callers likely share 120 a minute.
- What still holds: signed-in users count per user; registration has per-email and site-wide
  caps, and a human check.

† The fix is the platform team's, at the ingress, and would help every app behind it.

::: {.notes}
Confirmed 2026-06-15 with an off-VPN request: X-Forwarded-For arrives as 127.0.0.1, and so does
the socket peer. ProxyFix (src/webapp/run.py:86-95, PROXYFIX_X_FOR=1) cannot recover it. The fix
is ingress-nginx's forwarded headers (use-forwarded-headers, compute-full-forwarded-for) or the
proxy protocol at the load balancer; open, with no ticket found. Ben has no access to the
ingress logs. The API-key limit: src/webapp/utils/api_auth.py:220-224 keys on the IP because
Flask-Limiter runs before the decorator sets the key's identity; the limiter docstring and
RATE_LIMITING.md say per key (on the plan's fix-later list). The request log carries who= only
for signed-in users and keys (src/webapp/request_timing.py:136-138).
scripts/cirrus_weblog_audit.sh section 2 shows the symptom. Registration: Cloudflare Turnstile
on the final submit (#606).
:::

## The NRIT review: before we left the VPN {.smaller .fill scale="0.9"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
We asked NRIT's web team to review the whole tree before SAMuel went on the public internet.
182 items (15 P0, 55 P1, 112 P2), 54 strengths, and one headline: the app "fails open at the
boundaries".

Fixed in the first week:

- prod refuses the no-login and any-password switches
- permission gaps: the admin database view, allocation reads, resource details
- CSRF, the CSP and the other headers
- non-root pods, no service-account token; Redis reachable only from our pods

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Still open:

- collectors write zeros when they fail, and nothing alerts on it
- no error tracking; sign-in is not in the audit log
- CI actions pinned by tag, not hash; a personal token in four workflows
- single sign-on matches a user by name, not a stable ID

Fixed since: the secrets scanner pinned, the deploy branch locked, a read-only database
browser, API keys held to each route's permission.

A ZAP scan of 131 pages (June 15): no failures, 11 warnings; inline styles accepted.
:::
::::

## TL;DR - failing closed {.vcenter scale="1.15"}

- **A token on every browser write;** keys have no cookie to forge.
- **Scripts come only from us,** and a test keeps inline script out.
- **No third-party origins:** every asset is vendored and hash-pinned.
- **Limits per user,** and per IP, once **the platform forwards the address**.
- **The review's P0s are mostly closed;** the rest are **written down**.
